analysis: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis is primarily associated with deficiencies in anticoagulant proteins, particularly Protein C and Protein S. When warfarin is initiated, it inhibits vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, including Protein C and Protein S, leading to a transient hypercoagulable state. In individuals with Protein C deficiency, this can result in skin necrosis due to the inability to adequately regulate coagulation. Protein S deficiency also poses a risk, as it acts as a cofactor for Protein C. Hemophilia and Antithrombin III deficiency are not directly linked to this phenomenon, as they do not involve the same mechanisms of vitamin K inhibition and resultant hypercoagulability. Therefore, the most relevant options are Protein C deficiency and Protein S deficiency, with Protein C deficiency being the most commonly cited risk factor for warfarin-induced skin necrosis. Given this understanding, the best-supported option is Protein C deficiency.
